issues.title: Redesign macOS tweak workflow
issues.body:
## Summary

- Replace the duplicate header and full-screen side menu with a single desktop navigation bar.
- Present tweak install and removal as explicit, stateful actions; keep selected changes visible while searching.
- Move installation settings into the main workflow and refresh the CASDK layout.
- Keep the existing tweak IDs and compile handlers.

## Verification

- Built and launched the macOS x64 application.
- Checked navigation, tweak selection, Tools and Resources menus, and CASDK layout in the running app.
- Verified the app code signature and the generated DMG checksum.

The branch includes the macOS startup and Wi-Fi AP fix from #230 because the redesign was developed on top of it. Vehicle installation was not tested.
issues.author: herasymchyk-oleksii

issues.title: Fix macOS startup and Wi-Fi AP configuration errors
issues.body:
## Summary

- Skip the old updater when no update URL is configured, avoiding a startup failure on the packaged macOS app.
- Contain Google Translate initialization failures so its `Performance.measure` exception does not close the app.
- Write Wi-Fi AP settings to `02-start-wifiAP/wifiAP.config` after the recovery files finish copying. The previous literal `*-start-wifiAP` path caused `ENOENT`.

## Verification

- Built the macOS x64 app from the v2.8.6 source and verified its DMG checksum and app signature.
- Confirmed the packaged app contains the Wi-Fi AP fix.
- Ran a temporary-directory test that copies the recovery files and writes `wifiAP.config` to the expected directory.
- Ran `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

No vehicle installation was tested.

Changelog

Breaking Changes

Breaking changes will be documented here, and deprecation warnings added to JS code where possible, at least one major version before the change is made.

Types of Breaking Changes

This document uses the following convention to categorize breaking changes:

  • API Changed: An API was changed in such a way that code that has not been updated is guaranteed to throw an exception.
  • Behavior Changed: The behavior of Electron has changed, but not in such a way that an exception will necessarily be thrown.
  • Default Changed: Code depending on the old default may break, not necessarily throwing an exception. The old behavior can be restored by explicitly specifying the value.
  • Deprecated: An API was marked as deprecated. The API will continue to function, but will emit a deprecation warning, and will be removed in a future release.
  • Removed: An API or feature was removed, and is no longer supported by Electron.

Planned Breaking API Changes (30.0)

Behavior Changed: cross-origin iframes now use Permission Policy to access features

Cross-origin iframes must now specify features available to a given iframe via the allow attribute in order to access them.

See documentation for more information.

Removed: The --disable-color-correct-rendering switch

This switch was never formally documented but it's removal is being noted here regardless. Chromium itself now has better support for color spaces so this flag should not be needed.

Planned Breaking API Changes (29.0)

Behavior Changed: ipcRenderer can no longer be sent over the contextBridge

Attempting to send ipcRenderer as an object over the contextBridge will now result in an empty object on the receiving side of the bridge. This change was made to remove / mitigate a security footgun, you should not directly expose ipcRenderer or it's methods over the bridge. Instead provide a safe wrapper like below:

contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('app', {
  onEvent: (cb) => ipcRenderer.on('foo', (e, ...args) => cb(args))
})

Removed: renderer-process-crashed event on app

The renderer-process-crashed event on app has been removed. Use the new render-process-gone event instead.

Breaking Changes

Breaking changes will be documented here, and deprecation warnings added to JS code where possible, at least one major version before the change is made.

Types of Breaking Changes

This document uses the following convention to categorize breaking changes:

  • API Changed: An API was changed in such a way that code that has not been updated is guaranteed to throw an exception.
  • Behavior Changed: The behavior of Electron has changed, but not in such a way that an exception will necessarily be thrown.
  • Default Changed: Code depending on the old default may break, not necessarily throwing an exception. The old behavior can be restored by explicitly specifying the value.
  • Deprecated: An API was marked as deprecated. The API will continue to function, but will emit a deprecation warning, and will be removed in a future release.
  • Removed: An API or feature was removed, and is no longer supported by Electron.

Planned Breaking API Changes (23.0)

Removed: BrowserWindow scroll-touch-* events

The deprecated scroll-touch-begin, scroll-touch-end and scroll-touch-edge events on BrowserWindow have been removed. Instead, use the newly available input-event event on WebContents.

// Removed in Electron 23.0
win.on('scroll-touch-begin', scrollTouchBegin)
win.on('scroll-touch-edge', scrollTouchEdge)
win.on('scroll-touch-end', scrollTouchEnd)

// Replace with
win.webContents.on('input-event', (_, event) => {
if (event.type === 'gestureScrollBegin') {
scrollTouchBegin()
} else if (event.type === 'gestureScrollUpdate') {
scrollTouchEdge()
} else if (event.type === 'gestureScrollEnd') {
scrollTouchEnd()
}
})

Removed: webContents.incrementCapturerCount(stayHidden, stayAwake)

The webContents.incrementCapturerCount(stayHidden, stayAwake) function has been removed. It is now automatically handled by webContents.capturePage when a page capture completes.

const w = new BrowserWindow({ show: false })

// Removed in Electron 23
w.webContents.incrementCapturerCount()

v4.7.7 - February 15th, 2021

(POSSIBLY) BREAKING CHANGES:

  • the changes from version 4.6.0 now also apply in when using the compile-option "strict: true". Access to prototype properties is forbidden completely by default, specific properties or methods can be allowed via runtime-options. See #1633 for details. If you are using Handlebars as documented, you should not be accessing prototype properties from your template anyway, so the changes should not be a problem for you. Bumps [highlight.js](https://github.com/highlightjs/highlight.js) from 9.12.0 to 9.18.5.
Release notes

Sourced from highlight.js's releases.

10.3.2 - Oops, "Javascript".

Tiny tiny release, just to fix the website incorrectly not listing Javascript in the list of languages you could choose for a custom build. NPM and CDN build should not have been affected so 10.3.1 is effectively the same as 10.3.2 for those builds.

If you made a custom build from the website with 10.3 or 10.3.1 you may want to check and make sure it includes Javascript, and if not, build it again.

9.18.1 - Brrrrr, it’s freezing.

Quick release to resolve #2375

Changelog

Sourced from highlight.js's changelog.

Release v9.18.5

Version 9 has reached end-of-support and will not receive future updates or fixes.

Please see VERSION_10_UPGRADE.md and perhaps SECURITY.md.

  • enh: Post-install script can be disabled with HLJS_HIDE_UPGRADE_WARNING=yes
  • fix: Deprecation notice logged at library startup a console.log vs console.warn.
    • Notice only shown if actually highlighting code, not just requiring the library.
    • Node.js treats warn the same as error and that was problematic.
    • You (or perhaps your indirect dependency) may disable the notice with the hideUpgradeWarningAcceptNoSupportOrSecurityUpdates option
    • You can also set HLJS_HIDE_UPGRADE_WARNING=yes in your envionment to disable the warning

Example:

hljs.configure({
  hideUpgradeWarningAcceptNoSupportOrSecurityUpdates: true
})

Reference: highlightjs/highlight.js#2877

issues.title: carOS theme on Linux
issues.body:
The carOS theme does not work on Linux since the compile script tries to find ~/.config/MZD-AIO-TI/color-schemes/CarOS/jci.zip. And what is installed by the program there is ~/.config/MZD-AIO-TI/color-schemes/carOS/jci.zip. Since Linux is case-sensitive, it will not work.

Was easily solved by renaming the carOS directory to CarOS, but needs to be fixed in the MZD-AIO-TI.

Version tested was 2.8.5.

WIFI and Bluetooth uses the same frequency. Car system most likely going to have a one modem(using the same antenna) with WIFI and Bluetooth built in. Modem rapidly switches its radio between two if it is using both at the same time, but this should not be a problem since manufacture of those radios should handle it. However I haven't seen a inside of the Mazda system yet so I cannot tell whats going on. Other thing to note is, your phone or any other near by 2.4ghz radio could interfere when they disregard Bluetooth channels. 

Have you monitor the system usage during shuttering? You could enable the inlay by pressing Music + Back + Pwr/Mute. http://mazda3revolution.com/forums/2014-2017-mazda-3-skyactiv-audio-electronics/54722-accessing-infotainment-diagnostics-menu.html

comments.body:
Unfortunately In many of the CMUs before 2016, including my own, and most of the North American models the WiFi receiver is not properly shielded from electromagnetic interference caused by being to close to the Bluetooth adapter.  This guy said it best here:  http://whrl.pl/ReI3wR
> For those who have any Mazda model below model year 2016 (approximately) and MZD Connect.
> MMC has recognized that the CMU (Connectivity Master Unit, the thing that runs MZD) is defective when it comes to using Bluetooth and Wi-Fi (those who use and pay for Connected Services) together at the same time owners are seeing drop outs or connection issues with BT and or WiFi.
> Basically Visteon the makers of the CMU did not adequately 'shield' the two antenna inside CMU.
> The fix is a modified CMU only installed by your Mazda Dealer.
You must "complain" that you are having connection issues to these device services.
The Dealer may say it is your phone, or the firmware for CMU needs updating, 
this is a waste of time, the Firmware update does not fix a Hardware fault issue.

OK wow that is weird but here is what I am seeing from your video.
When you first launch the 4 processes I mentioned start up but all except for the main process crash.  So the processes that crash are the renderer, tray and the main window so now you are just left with the back-end main process which also holds the "app-lock" that keeps it a single instance app.  But every time you open it the main process is left behind and the window processes crash so there is something fishy going on because every subsequent main process should just exit automatically.

So thanks for letting me know that the crash server is not working correctly but you may notice that none of those logs says why it crashed.  I looked it up the error err_content_length_mismatch and there is an open issue in the module I use top update here: https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/issues/2534

I am pretty sure their servers are maintained very well so it is probably a problem with your network since updating windows didn't fix it.

comments.body:
@szsong, It seems to me that you may have a driver or software conflict between the 2 apps on your phone and the one installed on your MZD unit.. i doubt its a USB driver issue or even a cable issue.. the issue is with the AUDIO source not being handed over to the external source (the MZD).. are you aware that android auto has built in settings within the google settings of your phone?? as a suggestion, i recommend clearing the cache and clearing the data of both AA apps on your Android device. this will reset all settings and will help in narrowing down the cause of the problem.. 

in all honesty it basically just seems like a software conflict / issue.. or just simply wrong settngs

**EDIT** possible solution to fix your issue permanently is as follows..

1. unpair your Android BT with your MZD unit.
2. uninstall AIO AA app from Android device.. Be sure to clear all traces of the app (clear app data and app cache).
3. Reboot Android device.
4a. Make sure USB debugging is enabled on your Android device.
4b. Connect Android device to Cars USB hub (with phone icon).
5.  Set USB mode to MTP when prompted on your Android device.

try that and let me know how you go

One thing you can do right out of the box is add shadow with the "text colors"tweak or color to the text with the  "statusbar tweaks".  if you want to make edits yourself I would suggest not editing any JavaScript files especially SpeedBarTmplt.js because a mistake in that file will brick your system.  Plus everything youre asking for can be done with CSS and you can just add it to the end of this file with the rest of the statusbar speedometer CSS [StatusBarSpeedometer.css](https://github.com/Trevelopment/MZD-AIO/blob/master/app/files/tweaks/config/speedometer/jci/gui/apps/_speedometer/css/StatusBarSpeedometer.css)
the statusbar speedometer is actually on top of everything so it is not even under #barlayout.  I dont know how much you know about DOM but the only reason you can even see it with AA running is because it is outside of the main div that holds the GUI.  Anyways that CSS file should be self explanatory if you know CSS the main div id is `#SbSpeedo` with the main value in `#SbSpeedo .SbMain` and the 2 smaller values are `#SbSpeedo .SbVal1` and `#SbSpeedo .SbVal2`
You should probably add your custom CSS to the bottom of the file but I guess if you know what you are doing you can do whatever.  Also another tip I will offer is to use outlines instead of borders.  A border will increase the width & height of the div its around and might break some formatting if you don't compensate for that while outlines wont affect the div size.

comments.body:
There is a reason you have to get the upgraded USB hub to run the official AA/CP and that is because the stock hub has a shared USB port configuration while the upgraded hub changes that to an independent configuration. (actually I think stock might even split one bus between the 2 USB ports AND the SD card)
> Much like a data network, a USB port has limited bandwidth that it can share between devices. Usage varies from device to device. In an independent USB port, virtually all bandwidth – a total of 480 Mbps for 2.0 ports, and as much as 5 Gbps for 3.0 ports – is available for a single device. USB standards devote 10 percent of all data bandwidth to control, and reserve the rest for device use. In a shared environment, that bandwidth is shared between all devices. High-bandwidth peripherals, such as Web cameras or audio recorders [or a phone running Android Auto], may experience lower performance when connected to a shared USB port.

So let me ask, do you have anything using the other USB port?

comments.body:
Update to the headunit-wrapper fixing the test for a running headunit using "ps ax" to get the right 1/0 result. Startups are now more consistent both from cold start and re-start after a short stop. To be sure only one instance ever gets started there is a "killall -q -9 headunit" before launching a new instance. Still using a swapfile on a USB drive to maintain extra memory. Removing it caused some unexpected white screen freezes on warm startup. 

```
start_headunit()
{
  sed -i 's."wifiTransport": true."wifiTransport": false.g' /tmp/root/headunit.json
  killall -q -9 headunit
  sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches
  taskset 0xFFFFFFFF ionice -c 1 -n 0 nice -n -20 "${SCRIPTPATH}/headunit" "$@" >> ${LOGPATH} 2>&1 &
  echo "Start Headunit (USB Mode)"  >> ${LOGPATH}
}

# prevent conflict by Official AA
killall -q -9 aap_service carplayd L_jciCARPLAY L_jciAAPA

# loop forever. check for headunit running every 5 seconds
while true
do
  check_headunit=`ps ax|grep 'bin/headunit'|grep -v wrapper|grep -v grep|wc -l|awk '{print $1}'`
  [ $check_headunit -eq 0 ] && start_headunit
  sleep 5
done
```

Given that v70 is intended to use the new Hub it makes sense that there would be a difference.  One thing to note is there is a physical port difference as well between the two hubs with the newer android auto/carplay hub having two USB connection lines and the older ones only have one.  This may affect the naming convention and locations reported, I don't have the newer hub yet, but I am curious to see if I can create a rule that would allow the older hubs to be linked into the correct group and thereby enable the official android auto on them.  I also wonder if this project has had the ability to see the difference usb systemwise between the older(texas instrument hub) and the newer panasonic hub.

Starting with Android 10, Android Auto is built into the phone as a technology that enables your phone to connect to your car display. This means you no longer have to install a separate app from the Play Store to use Android Auto with your car display.  

If you don't have an Android Auto compatible car or prefer to access Android Auto on your phone screen, there are 3 options:

comments.body:
I was running into this exact issue, even after trying every UN/PW combo I could find. Below is what worked for me; I take no responsibility for any damage done yadda yadda.

**tl;dr:** I had to reflash my firmware which gave me root access, bypassing the UN/PW prompt. At that point I pasted the commands from [here ](https://mazdatweaks.com/id7/)and [here](https://mazdatweaks.com/serial/#process) and rebooted. Disconnected all the wires and mods are installing just fine via USB.

**Longer:**
1. Download the [ID7 Recovery XX](https://mazdatweaks.com/id7/) file from this link instead of compiling your own.
2. Download your [firmware here](https://my.hidrive.com/share/hsodpqja.l#$/) and copy it to the USB drive.
   - Note: You don't have to upgrade necessarily. You can re-flash the same version without issue.
   - Make sure to follow the PDF instructions on that site exactly.
3. While the firmware is updating, you will need to connect via SSH and wait for the update to complete.
4. I followed the PDF instructions exactly until the progress bar reached 100%.
4. At this point the screen will ask to reboot. Don't reboot just yet!
5. You should still be connected via SSH and can now enter: `cp -r /mnt/sd*/XX/* /mnt/data_persist/dev/bin/; chmod +x /mnt/data_persist/dev/bin/autorun; /mnt/data_persist/dev/bin/autorun`
6. Finally, [finish here](https://mazdatweaks.com/serial/#process) from step 10 onwards.
7. At this point I was able to use the AIO Tweaks app, compile what I wanted and install via USB.

comments.body:
There are some features that I wish this project could have supported. They are Android Auto features which the stock OEM can do - I can only tell these features because I installed OEM retro-kit on the family car, but not my car: 

1) Offer the Android Auto icon in the top left of the Mazda Connect home screen when you connect your phone as a short cut
2) Allow switching between Android Auto/Mazda Connect via 3 second hold of home button (instead of end call button)
3) When you are on any Mazda Connect screen, pressing the NAV button will navigate to google maps (if you have Mazda Navigation, then this shortcut does not apply)
4) If you are playing music from Android Auto but are on a Mazda Connect screen, pressing the MUSIC button will navigate to Android Auto media playing

With that being said, these are obviously features which I wish were implemented, but they are certainly not _needed_. It is completely reasonable to say that if I desire these things that much, I should just buy the upgrade kit and install it - and I may do that in the future. Anyways, this project has definitely served its purpose in providing a reliable means for modification of the Mazda Connect System. 

I realize how difficult it is to develop something like this in your free time @Trevelopment, and I thank you for your work on the project and sharing it with the world. This has provided value to my vehicle a lot, and I love using my car even more because of it.

I'll try with 70.00.352B.

Meanwhile, I unzipped several versions I have.

56.00.513B, 70.00.352B, 70.00.367A - all those have a step `passwdupdate` with the logic:

70x
```
# passwd needs updating everytime
cp /tmp/passwd /tmp/configtmp/passwd
```

but 56x:
```
if grep '^root:' /config-mfg/passwd ; then
    # passwd needs updating
    cp /tmp/passwd /tmp/configtmp/passwd
```

version 55x didn't have `passwdupdate` (at least NA one, I don't have EU 55x)

56x has `cmu` and `user` in passwd file (which is being copied during the install)

70x only has `cmu` user

`cmu` hashes are all the same (56/70)

`user` hash is much simpler, without the salt part, so I guess it's the `jci` one.

Today, before the update (being on 56), I could log in as `user`, and `root` with pw `jci`, didn't try the `cmu` user.

I guess we could "lost" the password for `root` even before 70, but password updating script was faulty.

Also, 70x updates has `neutralizeid7` script:

```
LAST_MESSAGE='"ID7_Recovery_Scripts" is not found.'
TARGET_DIR="/mnt/data_persist/dev/bin"
CONF_FILE="autorun"

if [ -e "${TARGET_DIR}/${CONF_FILE}" ]; then
    echo '"ID7_Recovery_Scripts" is found, so that getting them disabled...'
    LAST_MESSAGE="completed."
fi

if [ -d ${TARGET_DIR} ] ; then
    cd ${TARGET_DIR}
    ${DEBUG} rm -rf 00-*
    ${DEBUG} rm -rf 01-*
    ${DEBUG} rm -f adb
    ${DEBUG} rm -f 99-*.autorun
    ${DEBUG} rm -f ${CONF_FILE}
fi

echo ${LAST_MESSAGE}
echo ls -al ${TARGET_DIR} ; ls -al ${TARGET_DIR}

comments.body:
So, the issue is fixed.
If briefly, it was necessary to clear the **dumps** folder using the next command:
`# rm -rf ./tmp/mnt/data_persist/log/dumps/* ` 
and than the update/downgrade process had been continued. All in all, the CMU wrote the message "Version 70.00.352 software install was successful".

By the next step the ID7_Recovery_XX scripts had been installed 
`# cp -r /mnt/sd*/XX/* /mnt/data_persist/dev/bin/`
`# chmod +x /mnt/data_persist/dev/bin/autorun`
`# /mnt/data_persist/dev/bin/autorun`

So, the tweaks installs, the SSH works! The AndroidAuto (AA) is possible to install but it doesn't start after the connection of mobile. It's probably closed or well-secured for FW 70.00.XXX
If somebody knows how to lunch the AA using the mentioned FW, let me know, please.

Pulling out the SD card that is next to the USB sockets will help, BUT, the
processor is really not up to the job on the older Mazdas.  It wasn't
designed for that and even though it is only drawing the screen while your
phone does the calculations, it is not perfect.

What DOES help a lot is using an AA wireless module.  At least then your
phone is charging from a powerful charger plugged into the 12v port and
doesn't go into "conserve power mode" which slows down your phone, the USB
ports do not supply enough power to keep your phone happy during navigation
AND music.

I don't think mine stutters anymore.
It isn't as good as a newer car, but it's pretty good.

Oh one more thing, I only listen to downloaded playlists, albums, and
podcasts.  Streaming would bring it to it's knees.

Actually what it worked for me was just disabling the "media" option on the bluetooth pairing between my phone and the car. I've read something about in some mazda forums, where the Android Auto and the Car's bluetooth try to communicate at the same time with the bluetooth "media" so it is recommended to disable this in order to fully use Android auto (As AA itself comunicate completely with the phone through the android interface).

So, that basically solved my "black screen" issue.
Then i tried using it wireless following exactly those steps you wrote down, but it just didnt work. I didn't give any error, it just didn't work at all. I tried turning the hotspot on, connecting the car's wifi to the phone hotspot, then starting the headunit server, but AA didn't start. For me it just works through the USB cable.
